_comment: Shared 28-bit callsign PACKING vectors, asserted from both languages.
Distinct from callsign_vectors.json, which pins the structural VALIDATION rule the
transmit gate applies. This file pins the encoding: what integer a callsign occupies in
the 28-bit field, and whether it survives a round trip.
It exists because a priori decoding asserts those 28 bits as certain. src/dsp/apDecode.ts
derives them by packing a message and reading its bits, and z30_dsp/ap_decode.py derives
them from z30_dsp/message_codec.py. If the two packers disagreed by one integer, the
Python benchmark would be measuring the gain of a hypothesis the browser never forms.
'round_trips' is what decides whether a callsign may be used as a priori knowledge at all:
a call that takes the generic Base-37 fallback packs to an integer that does not unpack
back to it, so asserting those bits would assert a callsign nobody transmitted. This is
WSJT-X's ft8apset rule (pack a dummy message, unpack it, and refuse unless msg.eq.msgchk).
Generated from src/dsp/z30Codec.ts, which shipped first. Asserted by

vectors.why: lower case is upper-cased before packing
portable prefix: takes the Base-37 fallback, does NOT round-trip
